title: Pin the plain paseo send to --behavior interrupt
action: Per decision ebda4a72 (paseo-017-compat D1). In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/paseo.rs change fn send_argv (about line 500) so it returns ["send", id, "--behavior", "interrupt", "--no-wait", "--", text], the same shape as send_steer_argv with interrupt in place of steer. Update the unit test that asserts send_argv (about line 1508) to the new argv. Do not change send_steer_argv or any caller in run.rs; both callers (run.rs about 4444 round brief pointer, about 5000 and 5053 idle nudge) pick up the new argv through send_argv. Then sync docs/knowledge/areas/bee-herding/the-paseo-channel.md in the same commit: where it describes the plain send (round pointer / nudge), state that bee passes --behavior interrupt explicitly; add a short 'Paseo 0.17' paragraph with these facts and cite paseo-017-compat D1 ebda4a72 and D2 b298b6e6 in the prose and in the frontmatter decisions list: since Paseo 0.17 the send default depends on the sender (queue for an agent sender with PASEO_AGENT_ID, interrupt for a person); bee sends as a person because it scrubs PASEO_AGENT_ID from every paseo call except the worker run; the 0.17.3 daemon refuses --behavior queue from a non-agent sender; the send receipt guidance exists only for queued agent sends, so bee does not parse it; paseo ls --json now carries workspaceId and labels, which bee does not read; messages from other agents (a worker's notification to its lead) now wait for the lead's current turn to end. Leave the frontmatter status alone unless the knowledge check requires otherwise. No code comments.
